en.title: Group Defective Weight & Waste Sales Auto-Consolidation System
en.summary: Upload waste analysis spreadsheets from multiple plants in different Excel formats at once; the system automatically recognizes plant, product, and subtotal data, fills them into the group consolidation template, and produces a downloadable report, cutting manual copying and cross-checking time.
en.author: Chiao-Kuei Hsu
en.region: Group plants across Taiwan, Mainland China, and Southeast Asia
en.problem_background: Each plant's monthly waste analysis spreadsheets mix old and new Excel formats, with inconsistent plant names, product sheets, and column layouts. Auditors had to check each file one by one and manually fill in the group consolidation sheet, which was slow and error-prone.
en.core_problem: How to correctly identify each plant and product during a batch upload, handle duplicate files, naming variations, and unnumbered plants, and write the data into the correct location in the original consolidation template.
en.solution: Built a web-based batch consolidation tool that automatically reads .xls and .xlsx files, identifies plants and products, locates subtotal rows and previews the results, then dynamically writes data based on the target sheet's plant sections and product names, preserving the original formatting and formulas.
process: Select and upload each plant's Excel report at once.
The system identifies plants, products, subtotal rows, and weight columns.
The user reviews the preview and duplicate-file warnings.
After confirmation, download the consolidated report based on the group template.

features.desc: Finds the target row by sheet name, reducing impact from template changes.

features.desc: Lists duplicate source files and unconfigured items.

Built the parsing, dynamic matching, anomaly-check, and export rules.
Assisted with development, test cases, debugging, and deployment verification.

Completed the online analysis, preview, error-alert, and Excel download workflow.

value.name: For the Company
value.desc: Establishes a consistent, traceable consolidation process, improving group data quality and operational efficiency.

zh.title: 季度總表歷史處理方式自動彙整工具
zh.summary: 透過 Excel VBA 自動整理季度追蹤總表，依物料號碼比對歷史資料並帶入前期處理方式，同時檢查並補齊追蹤及發信欄位，降低人工查找與複製貼上的時間。
zh.author: 陳姸惠
zh.region: 台灣
zh.problem_background: 季度追蹤總表需參考前期資料，人工逐筆搜尋物料號碼、查找歷史處理方式並複製到新一期總表，資料量增加後容易耗時，也可能發生漏查或貼錯資料。
zh.core_problem: 每季皆需重複進行相同的歷史資料查找與欄位整理工作，且不同部門資料分散於多個工作表，人工比對效率低，也增加資料錯置風險。
zh.solution: 以 Excel VBA 建立自動彙整功能，讓使用者選擇最新總表及歷史來源檔後，自動辨識期間、逐工作表比對物料號碼，並將歷史處理方式帶回最新總表。
process: 選擇最新一期總表，系統先檢查各工作表必要追蹤欄位。
若缺少「處理方式追蹤確認」或「是否發信」，自動於「廠別」右側補上。
選擇欲參考的歷史來源檔案，系統由檔名自動辨識年月。
依研發、製蓋、製瓶、業務等部門尋找對應工作表。
以物料號碼比對歷史資料，將前期處理方式帶入最新總表。
完成後自動儲存，並顯示成功、未找到及重複物料筆數。

features.desc: 自動檢查「處理方式追蹤確認」及「是否發信」欄位，缺少時自動補齊。

features.name: 重複資料處理

features.desc: 完成後統計成功對應、找不到物料、重複物料及未處理工作表。

協助產生及反覆調整 VBA 程式，處理欄位辨識、跨工作表比對及例外狀況。
依實際測試結果協助除錯，逐步調整成符合使用者既有 Excel 作業方式的工具。

results: 將原本逐工作表、逐筆查找歷史資料的作業改為一次自動處理。
自動完成物料號碼比對及歷史處理方式回填，降低人工複製貼上的錯誤風險。
統一檢查總表必要追蹤欄位，減少不同工作表欄位缺漏問題。

extensions: 可延伸至其他定期需引用前期資料的追蹤表、稽核表或專案管理表。
可依不同欄位名稱調整比對條件，應用於跨月份、跨季度或跨年度資料彙整。
後續可串接發信名單整理功能，將需通知的資料依單位自動分類。
limitations: 來源檔名需包含可辨識的年月資訊；若無法辨識，需由使用者手動輸入年月。

目前部門工作表以研發、製蓋、製瓶、業務等既定名稱關鍵字進行辨識。
執行前仍建議確認來源檔案及目標總表版本，避免選錯期間資料。
zh.success_key: 先釐清既有 Excel 人工作業規則，再以不改變使用習慣為原則進行自動化，讓工具直接嵌入原本的季度總表流程，降低使用門檻。

en.title: Automated Quarterly History Lookup Tool
en.summary: An Excel VBA tool that automatically organizes the quarterly tracking master sheet, matching material numbers against historical records to pull in prior handling methods, while checking and filling required tracking and notification columns to cut down manual lookup and copy-pasting.
en.author: Yen-Hui Chen
en.problem_background: The quarterly tracking master sheet needs to reference prior-period data. Staff manually search for each material number, look up its historical handling method, and copy it into the new sheet — as data volume grows this becomes time-consuming and prone to missed lookups or misplaced entries.
en.core_problem: The same historical lookup and column formatting work must be repeated every quarter, with data for different departments scattered across multiple worksheets — manual comparison is inefficient and increases the risk of misplaced data.
en.solution: Built an Excel VBA tool that lets users select the latest master sheet and a historical source file; the tool automatically detects the period, matches material numbers sheet by sheet, and brings the prior handling method back into the latest master sheet.
process: Select the latest master sheet; the tool first checks each worksheet for the required tracking columns.
If "Handling Method Tracking Confirmation" or "Notification Sent" is missing, it is automatically added to the right of the "Factory" column.
Select the historical source file to reference; the tool auto-detects the year/month from the file name.
Locates the corresponding worksheet by department (R&D, Cap Manufacturing, Bottle Manufacturing, Sales, etc.).
Matches material numbers against historical data and pulls the prior handling method into the latest master sheet.
Saves automatically when done and displays counts of successful matches, not-found items, and duplicate materials.

features.name: Historical Data Matching
features.desc: Automatically finds matching prior-period records by material number and pulls in the handling method.

features.name: Automatic Period Detection
features.desc: Detects the year/month from the source file name and creates the corresponding historical handling method column.

features.name: Automatic Worksheet Mapping
features.desc: Automatically locates source data by department, such as R&D, Cap Manufacturing, Bottle Manufacturing, and Sales.

features.name: Tracking Column Check
features.desc: Automatically checks the "Handling Method Tracking Confirmation" and "Notification Sent" columns and fills them in when missing.

features.name: Duplicate Handling
features.desc: When the same material number appears more than once, takes the first match, following VLOOKUP-style logic.

features.name: Execution Reporting
features.desc: After completion, reports counts of successful matches, not-found materials, duplicate materials, and unprocessed worksheets.

ai_usage: Helped break down the manual quarterly consolidation process into automatable data-processing logic.
Helped generate and iteratively refine the VBA code to handle column detection, cross-sheet matching, and exceptions.
Helped debug based on real test results, gradually tuning the tool to fit the user's existing Excel workflow.

tools.name: Microsoft Excel
tools.desc: The main working environment for the source master sheet, historical data, and final consolidated results.

tools.name: VBA
tools.desc: Handles file selection, column checks, cross-sheet data matching, data backfill, and result reporting.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.desc: Helped break down requirements, write the VBA code, and analyze and adjust functionality based on testing.

results: Replaced the sheet-by-sheet, entry-by-entry historical lookup process with a single automated run.
Automated material number matching and historical handling method backfill, reducing the risk of manual copy-paste errors.
Standardized checks on the master sheet's required tracking columns, reducing missing columns across worksheets.

value.name: For the Requesting Unit
value.desc: Reduces time spent on repeated quarterly lookups and data copying, freeing staff to focus on data verification and follow-up.

value.name: For the Company
value.desc: Standardizes a fixed, repetitive Excel task, reducing manual errors and improving data organization efficiency.

extensions: Can be extended to other tracking sheets, audit sheets, or project management sheets that regularly reference prior-period data.
Matching criteria can be adjusted for different column names, applying it across months, quarters, or years.
Can later be connected to a notification list feature to automatically categorize records that need notification by unit.
limitations: The source file name must contain a recognizable year/month; otherwise the user must enter it manually.
Each worksheet must have required fields such as "Material Number" for automatic matching to work.
Department worksheets are currently identified using fixed name keywords: R&D, Cap Manufacturing, Bottle Manufacturing, Sales, etc.
Users should still confirm the source file and target master sheet version before running, to avoid selecting the wrong period.
en.success_key: Clarified the existing manual Excel workflow rules first, then automated without changing user habits, embedding the tool directly into the existing quarterly master sheet process to lower the barrier to adoption.

zh.title: 報價底價檢查系統
zh.summary: 透過瀏覽器上傳訂單成本登記表 PDF，自動辨識品名、規格、銷售單價與備註價格，依主管核准底價找出低價報價及待確認品項。
zh.author: 徐喬奎
zh.region: 東南亞／印尼
zh.problem_background: 訂單成本表含多種產品、料號與備註價格，主管需人工逐筆核對業務報價，耗時且容易遺漏低於底價或成本關係不合理的品項。

en.title: Quotation Floor Price Checker
en.summary: Upload order cost sheets (PDF) in the browser to automatically identify product names, specs, sale prices, and remark-based pricing, then flag any quote below the manager-approved floor price or any item that still needs review.
en.author: Chiao-Kuei Hsu
en.problem_background: Order cost sheets contain many products, material codes, and remark-based prices. Managers had to manually check every sales quote line by line, which was time-consuming and prone to missing quotes below the floor price or with inconsistent cost relationships.
en.core_problem: As material codes keep growing, setting a price range for each one individually causes maintenance effort to balloon. Remarks can also mix original price, adjusted price, customer-supplied material, and different pricing methods at the same time.
en.solution: Group products by product name and spec into shared price groups, each maintaining only a single minimum sale price. PDFs are parsed entirely in the browser, automatically checking the quoted price against the floor price and the remark-based price relationships, and surfacing only the exceptions.
process: Manager sets the minimum sale price for each product group
User uploads one or more order cost sheet PDFs
System identifies product name, spec, material code, quoted price, and remarks
Automatic comparison against price groups and remark rules
Items below the floor price or that cannot be classified are shown together

features.name: Batch PDF checking
features.desc: Upload multiple order cost sheets at once and parse them entirely in the browser

features.name: Product name/spec grouping
features.desc: Products of the same type share one floor price; new material codes require no extra setup

features.name: Floor price checking
features.desc: Finds sales quotes that fall below the manager-approved floor price

features.name: Remark rule checking
features.desc: Automatically compares five remark-based relationships — average purchase price, average inventory cost, OEM fee cost, imported cap purchase requests, and customer-supplied material — with no manual price entry needed

features.name: Exception list
features.desc: Shows the order, page, material code, actual quote, floor price, and reason for each flagged item

ai_usage: Helped analyze order PDFs across different versions to organize product categories, price fields, and remark rules

Helped design the parsing logic, exception-detection flow, and user interface

tools.desc: Version control and collaboration history

results: Completed v0.2.0 test version and deployed it to Vercel
Validated against 5 real PDFs covering 46 line items, all of which could be classified into price groups by name and spec
Simplified per-material-code price ranges into a single floor price across 21 shared groups (Labels 4, Caps 4, Empty Bottles 9, Filling OEM 4)
Supports four product categories: labels, caps, empty bottles, and filling OEM
Added an "imported cap purchase request" check among the remark-based price relationships — since it isn't compared cross-currency, it's flagged for manual review rather than auto-matched

value.name: For sales teams
value.desc: Quickly catches quotes below the floor price before submission for approval, reducing back-and-forth confirmation

value.name: For management
value.desc: Reviews exception reasons in one place, reducing the burden of manually checking every line and maintaining pricing rules

value.name: For the company
value.desc: Reduces the risk of underpriced orders and margin loss, and establishes a quotation-checking process that can keep scaling

extensions: Can be extended to other overseas plants, customers, and different order cost sheet formats
Can add a shared backend, manager login, price versioning, effective dates, and change history
Can be extended to Excel quotations, purchase orders, and cost anomaly checks
limitations: Floor price settings are currently stored in a single browser and not yet shared across devices
Major PDF format changes or scanned-image PDFs may require new parsing rules or OCR
Unclassified new products are flagged as pending review rather than automatically approved
Currency and units follow the PDF's original values; no exchange-rate or unit conversion is performed
en.success_key: Replaced per-material-code setup with product name/spec grouping, and kept PDF processing entirely in the browser — reducing maintenance effort while preserving accuracy and document confidentiality.

zh.title: 宏全國際集團 THC 尾牙抽獎系統前台美化與流程優化
zh.summary: 本次協助資訊單位針對宏全國際集團尾牙抽獎網站進行前台畫面美化與部分現場流程調整。原系統已具備人員匯入、獎項設定、資格限制、抽獎與結果匯出等功能，本次不重寫既有抽獎邏輯，而是聚焦於抽獎主畫面、獎項選擇流程、抽獎動畫、得獎結果彈窗與舞台主題切換，讓系統更適合正式活動現場投影與觀眾觀看。
zh.author: 陳姸惠
zh.region: 宏全國際集團尾牙活動現場
zh.problem_background:
資訊單位原本已完成尾牙抽獎系統的主要功能，但抽獎頁面仍較接近後台操作介面，現場使用時不容易讓操作者快速判斷下一步，也不夠適合直接投影給觀眾觀看。

原本的抽獎畫面將獎項、控制項與結果資訊集中在同一頁，當獎項數量增加時畫面容易擁擠；設定完成後的抽獎入口也不夠醒目。抽獎動畫與得獎彈窗的視覺呈現較簡化，缺少正式活動的舞台感與中獎氛圍。此外，原先背景圖與 LOGO 上傳等設定容易增加操作干擾，因此本次協助資訊單位改善網站前台視覺與部分現場流程。
zh.core_problem: 本次需求的核心不是重做抽獎系統，而是在不影響既有抽獎規則的前提下，讓網站更適合正式活動現場使用。需要改善操作者從設定到開始抽獎的動線，讓獎項選擇、抽獎動畫與得獎結果更清楚；同時提供不同風格的視覺主題，讓抽獎畫面不只侷限於傳統金紅紫企業晚會風格。
zh.solution:
本次修正將抽獎主畫面重新整理為獎項牆流程，操作者在設定完成後可直接進入獎項卡片選擇畫面，選定獎項後進入全畫面抽獎機動畫，動畫結束後直接跳出得獎結果彈窗。已抽出的獎項會顯示完成狀態，並提供中獎名單與重新抽籤操作。

視覺上移除不必要的背景圖與 LOGO 設定，改以系統內建舞台主題控制整體風格。抽獎機動畫加入玻璃罩、底座、正圓球體、舞台光束與金幣效果，並新增多套主題色系，套用範圍涵蓋抽獎主畫面、獎項牆、抽獎機、得獎彈窗與展示畫面。
process: 釐清資訊單位需求，確認本次重點為網站美化與抽獎流程優化，不更動原有抽獎設定與資格限制邏輯。
盤點現有 Draw 頁、設定頁、得獎彈窗與展示畫面的使用痛點。
將抽獎主畫面改為獎項牆，讓操作者先選擇本輪要抽出的獎項。
調整抽獎流程為一次抽出該獎項所有剩餘名額，降低現場等待時間。
為已抽出獎項新增完成狀態，並保留中獎名單與重新抽籤操作。
將「設定完成，開始抽獎」移至更醒目的位置，改善設定後的操作動線。
移除右上角容易混淆的抽獎導覽按鈕，讓正式入口更清楚。
升級抽獎機動畫，加入玻璃罩、球體、底座、光束與金幣效果。
新增舞台主題選擇，並讓主題套用到抽獎端主要畫面。

en.title: Taiwan Hon Chuan (THC) Year-End Lottery System: Front-of-House Redesign and Flow Optimization
en.summary: Helped the IT unit redesign the front-of-house screens and adjust part of the on-site flow for Taiwan Hon Chuan Group's year-end party lottery site. The existing system already handled participant import, prize setup, eligibility rules, drawing, and result export; this effort did not rewrite the drawing logic, but focused on the main draw screen, prize-selection flow, draw animation, winner result popup, and stage theme switching, making the system better suited for on-site projection and audience viewing at a formal event.
en.author: Chen Yen-Hui
en.region: Taiwan Hon Chuan Group year-end party venue
en.problem_background:
The IT unit had already built the core functions of the lottery system, but the draw page still resembled a back-office control panel — on site, operators could not quickly judge the next step, and the screen was not well suited for direct projection to the audience.

The original draw screen packed prizes, controls, and result information onto a single page, so the layout became crowded as the number of prizes grew, and the entry point to start a draw after setup was not prominent enough. The draw animation and winner popup were visually simplified, lacking the stage presence and celebratory feel of a formal event. In addition, the original background-image and logo upload settings added unnecessary operational friction, so this effort helped the IT unit improve the front-of-house visuals and part of the on-site flow.
en.core_problem: The core of this request was not to rebuild the lottery system, but to make the site better suited for a formal on-site event without affecting the existing drawing rules. The flow from setup to starting a draw needed to be clearer for operators, with prize selection, draw animation, and winner results all easier to follow — while also offering different visual themes so the draw screen would not be limited to the traditional gold-red-purple corporate banquet look.
en.solution:
The main draw screen was reorganized into a prize-wall flow: once setup is complete, the operator goes straight to a prize-card selection screen, and after picking a prize, a full-screen draw-machine animation plays before the winner result popup appears automatically. Prizes that have already been drawn show a completed status, with a winner list and re-draw action available.

Visually, the unnecessary background-image and logo settings were removed in favor of built-in stage themes controlling the overall look. The draw-machine animation now includes a glass dome, base, perfectly round balls, stage light beams, and coin effects, with several new theme color sets applied consistently across the main draw screen, prize wall, draw machine, winner popup, and display screen.
process: Clarified the IT unit's requirements and confirmed this round would focus on visual redesign and draw-flow optimization, without changing the existing draw settings or eligibility logic.

zh.region: 泰國廠區（Hon Chuan FD Packaging）

en.title: Quality & Waste Tracking Dashboard (Printing BK04-06 & Assembly BL06-08)
en.summary: Used AI (Claude) to automatically turn the weekly raw Excel quality and waste data from the printing (BK04-06) and assembly (BL06-08) machines into a bilingual (Thai/English) interactive dashboard, covering both the "quality" side (compared by operator/machine/defect type) and the "waste" side (compared by machine/shift/film material/operator), helping the floor and management quickly locate the source of problems and focus improvement efforts.
en.author: Pongwish Kampetch
en.status: Completed, in continuous weekly use (the assembly process has been packaged as a reusable Claude skill)
en.problem_background: The printing machines (BK04-06) and assembly machines (BL06-08) generate a large amount of quality and waste data every week. In the past this was recorded only in raw Excel sheets, making it hard for management and floor supervisors to quickly see which operator, which machine, which defect/film type, or which shift was the main issue — and there was no effective way to track weekly trends or anomalies for specific customers.
en.core_problem: The data volume was large and scattered across multiple weekly Excel files, and the printing and assembly processes had different data structures, making manual organization time-consuming — while also needing to support both Thai- and English-speaking users (floor staff and expatriate supervisors) at the same time.
en.solution: Had AI (Claude) read the printing and assembly processes' separate weekly quality/waste raw Excel data, automatically compiling it into KPI cards, charts by operator/machine/shift/film material, defect Pareto analysis, and filterable detail tables, producing a bilingual HTML dashboard. The assembly portion was further packaged into a reusable Claude skill, so future updates only require uploading the new week's data for the dashboard to be generated automatically.
process: Export the weekly quality/waste raw Excel data for printing (BK04-06) or assembly (BL06-08).
Have AI compile it by machine, shift, operator, and film material/defect type.
AI produces a bilingual interactive HTML dashboard (KPI cards, charts, Pareto analysis, filterable detail tables).
The assembly process is additionally packaged as a Claude skill for repeated weekly use.
Produce a month-over-month comparison PPTX summary as needed.

The assembly process can now be regenerated weekly with a fixed skill, without needing to re-communicate requirements.

value.desc: Reduces material waste and production costs, and establishes a sustainable quality/waste tracking model that can be replicated in other processes.

extensions: The same model can be extended to quality and waste tracking in other processes (such as cutting or perforation).

Could be integrated with an OEE/production monitoring dashboard in the future to form a single combined weekly meeting report.

The printing and assembly logic is currently maintained as two separate sets — if the data structure changes, both need to be updated in sync.
en.success_key: Custom-building the compilation logic separately for the printing and assembly processes' different data structures, presenting both the quality and waste dimensions under one unified tracking model, and packaging the highly repetitive assembly workflow into a reusable Claude skill.

zh.title: 生產計畫密度檢核工具（HCFD Planning — เช็คความแน่นแพลน）
zh.summary: 以訂單交期回推每日應開始生產日期，並自動計算每日產能佔用率（正常/加班兩種模式），以顏色（綠/橘/紅）呈現產線「鬆／緊／爆單」狀況的排程檢核工具，協助生產計畫在新單進來時快速判斷能否如期交貨，並提前找出撞期風險日。
zh.author: Pongwish Kampetch
zh.status: 已完成，工具與 Excel 資料庫持續使用中
zh.region: 泰國廠區（Hon Chuan FD Packaging）
zh.problem_background: 過去業務或計畫人員在接新單時，僅憑經驗判斷產線是否有空檔可接單，缺乏系統化的每日產能佔用檢核，容易發生多筆訂單交期集中在同一天、造成單日產能暴衝、進而導致延遲交貨或被迫緊急加班的情況。
zh.core_problem: 如何在訂單交期資訊分散、且訂單量大（百筆以上）的情況下，快速且視覺化地看出哪些日期產能已經吃緊或超載，並在新單洽談階段就能預估可行的交貨日期。
zh.solution: 建立一套「訂單 → 依交期與產能回推應開始生產日期 → 每日產能佔用率視覺化日曆」的 Excel 工具，並搭配獨立的 HCFD Planning 網頁工具（HCFD_Planning.html），支援上傳訂單 Excel 後自動依交期排序、計算正常/加班兩種產能模式下的可行性，並標示逾期風險與可用日期建議。
process: 業務/計畫人員將新訂單資料（交期、客戶、數量、生產工時）輸入「ออเดอร์」訂單清單
系統依交期、Buffer 天數（QC/出貨準備）自動回推「應開始生產日期」
「ปฏิทิน」日曆分頁依應開始生產日期，加總每日所需生產工時，並依占用率（<85% 綠、85–100% 橘、>100% 紅）自動上色
「คำนวณวันส่ง」分頁可讓使用者輸入新單所需工時，直接試算最快可交付日期
「ตั้งค่า」「วันหยุด」分頁可調整產能參數（正常/OT 每日工時、Buffer 天數、判斷門檻）與公司假日曆
另有獨立 HCFD_Planning.html 網頁版，支援上傳訂單 Excel 並提供逾期標示、搜尋、語言切換等互動功能

en.title: Planning Tightness Check Tool (HCFD Planning — เช็คความแน่นแพลน)
en.summary: A scheduling check tool that works backward from order due dates to determine each day's required production start date, automatically calculates daily capacity utilization under two modes (normal / overtime), and shows the production line's "loose / tight / overloaded" status with color coding (green/orange/red) — helping production planning quickly judge whether a new order can be delivered on time and flagging at-risk dates in advance.
en.author: Pongwish Kampetch
en.status: Completed, tool and Excel database in continuous use
en.problem_background: In the past, when sales or planning staff took on a new order, they judged whether the production line had open capacity purely by experience, with no systematic daily capacity check. This often led to multiple orders' due dates clustering on the same day, causing a spike in that day's required capacity, which in turn caused late deliveries or forced emergency overtime.
en.core_problem: With order due-date information scattered across records and a large order volume (100+ orders), how can tight or overloaded capacity dates be identified quickly and visually, and a feasible delivery date be estimated as early as the new-order negotiation stage?
en.solution: Built an Excel tool that works through "order → work backward from due date and capacity to the required production start date → a visualized daily-capacity-utilization calendar," paired with a standalone HCFD Planning web tool (HCFD_Planning.html) that lets users upload an order Excel file and automatically sorts by due date, calculates feasibility under both normal and overtime capacity modes, and flags overdue risk with suggested available dates.
process: Sales/planning staff enter new order data (due date, customer, quantity, production hours) into the "ออเดอร์" order list.
The system automatically works backward from the due date and buffer days (QC/shipping prep) to determine the "required production start date."
The "ปฏิทิน" calendar tab sums the required production hours per day by production start date and auto-colors each day by utilization (<85% green, 85–100% orange, >100% red).
The "คำนวณวันส่ง" tab lets users enter the hours needed for a new order and instantly estimate the earliest feasible delivery date.
The "ตั้งค่า" and "วันหยุด" tabs let users adjust capacity parameters (normal/OT daily hours, buffer days, thresholds) and the company holiday calendar.
A standalone HCFD_Planning.html web version is also available, supporting order Excel upload with overdue flagging, search, and language switching.

features.desc: Capacity, buffer days, tight/overload thresholds, and the company holiday calendar can all be configured.

Produced visual charts to help quickly read when and how severely capacity becomes tight.
Developed a standalone interactive web tool (HCFD_Planning.html) for quick lookups without needing to open Excel.

results: Can pinpoint the key dates with the highest capacity utilization among hundreds of orders — and the cause — within seconds (e.g. a single day reaching 246% of normal capacity).
Planning staff can quickly estimate a feasible delivery date at the new-order negotiation stage, reducing cases where a scheduling conflict is only discovered afterward.
Established a reusable, self-configurable standardized scheduling check tool.

extensions: The same scheduling logic can be extended to other processes or lines with a clear capacity ceiling.
Can be integrated with MES/production monitoring dashboards, feeding actual output data back into the capacity utilization calculation.
Automatic early-warning notifications could be added in the future to proactively alert planning staff when a new order is entered and a scheduling conflict risk is detected.
limitations: Order data still needs to be entered or uploaded manually into Excel/the web tool; it is not yet connected to an ERP/order system for automatic sync.
Capacity parameters (normal/OT hours, buffer days) must be set manually and kept up to date — if actual line conditions change, they need to be adjusted in sync.
Data needs to be updated regularly; an outdated order database cannot reflect the true current capacity situation.
en.success_key: Standardizing and visualizing the "due date → capacity" scheduling judgment logic so that non-technical sales and planning staff can spot at-risk dates at a glance, while keeping both the Excel and web versions available to balance flexibility and convenience.

en.title: Automated Label Printing System (Standalone Label Printing — Replacing Handwritten Roll-Core Labels)
en.summary: A browser-based automated label printing system that replaces the manual, handwritten roll-core labeling process on the shop floor. Operators use a Windows tablet connected to a Zebra printer to print labels directly, cutting down transcription errors and time, while also laying the data groundwork for a future MES integration.
en.author: Pongwish Kampetch
en.status: Development and on-site rollout completed (including training materials and a management proposal)
en.problem_background: On the BF process floor, roll-core label information used to be filled in by hand, which was prone to illegible handwriting, transcription errors, or incomplete information — making later traceability difficult, and the data could not be directly accumulated in digital form for downstream systems such as MES.
en.core_problem: How to digitize the handwritten labeling process without adding to floor staff's workload, while making the resulting data structured enough to be connected to production systems in the future.
en.solution: Developed a browser-based standalone label printing tool. Floor staff operate it on a Windows tablet, entering the roll number, pass (L/M/R/S/H), splice count, and other information step by step, then print the label directly via a Zebra printer. Every print is kept as a history record to serve as the data foundation for a future MES system, along with operator training materials and a management rollout proposal.
process: Floor staff open the label printing system on a tablet and select or create a job.
They enter the roll number, pass, splice count, and other information following the on-screen steps.
The system prints the label directly via a Zebra printer.
The system keeps a searchable print history.
Combined with training and a management proposal, the tool was formally rolled out for floor use.

value.desc: Floor operations are more standardized, reducing traceability difficulties caused by handwriting errors.

en.success_key: Starting from a real shop-floor pain point (error-prone handwritten labels), designing a simple, easy-to-use step-by-step interface, and pairing it with training to complete a smooth on-site rollout — while laying the data groundwork for a future MES integration in advance.

zh.author: Pongwish Kampetch
zh.status: 已完成，持續每週／每日更新使用中（目前版本 v10）

zh.problem_background: 每日各機台（印刷 BK 系列、組裝 BL 系列）都會產生大量生產與品質原始資料，過去需人工彙整成 OEE（Availability、Performance、Quality）指標，才能在每週 Printing/Assembly KPI 週會上呈現，過程耗時且容易出錯，也難以快速比較不同時間區間的趨勢。

en.title: Production Monitoring Dashboard & Weekly KPI Meeting (Production Dashboard + Weekly Printing/Assembly KPI Meeting, incl. OEE)
en.summary: Used AI (Claude) to automatically turn the printing and assembly departments' daily/weekly raw production Excel data into standardized OEE metrics (Availability, Performance, Quality) and a production monitoring dashboard, serving as the core report for the weekly Printing/Assembly KPI meeting.
en.author: Pongwish Kampetch
en.status: Completed, in continuous weekly/daily use (currently version v10)
en.problem_background: Every day, each machine (printing BK series, assembly BL series) generates a large amount of raw production and quality data. In the past this had to be manually compiled into OEE metrics (Availability, Performance, Quality) for presentation at the weekly Printing/Assembly KPI meeting — a process that was time-consuming, error-prone, and made it hard to quickly compare trends across different time periods.
en.core_problem: Data was scattered across multiple daily Excel reports and needed to be compiled by machine and operator, then converted using the standard OEE formula (A 25%, P 15%, Q 60% weighting) — manual compilation could not keep up with the fixed weekly cadence of the KPI review meeting.
en.solution: Had AI (Claude) read the raw daily production Excel data, automatically compiling output, time, speed, and defect rate by machine/operator, and calculating Availability, Performance, Quality, and the weighted OEE, producing a production monitoring dashboard with cross-month trend comparison. The compiled results became the standard report output for the weekly Printing/Assembly KPI meeting.
process: Export the daily production and quality raw Excel data for the printing (BK) and assembly (BL) machines.
Have AI compile Good/Bad output, hours, speed, and defect rate by machine/operator.
AI calculates OEE using the formula (A 25% + P 15% + Q 60% weighting).
Produces a production monitoring dashboard (including multi-month trends and threshold/standard checks).
Used as the main reporting material at the weekly Printing/Assembly KPI meeting.

zh.title: 製造執行系統整體規劃草案（HCFD MES — Full System Draft）
zh.summary: 針對 Shrink Sleeve／Label／Convert 產線規劃的完整 MES（Manufacturing Execution System）系統草案，涵蓋從資料輸入、生產排程、機台佇列、工單路徑、現場操作、品質與缺陷、稼動與停機監控到報表的完整模組，目前已完成介面草案設計，其中「生產總覽（Production Overview）」模組已可呈現 Plan/Actual/Waste/OEE 即時看板與依站別的在製品（WIP）看板。
zh.author: Pongwish Kampetch
zh.status: 系統草案設計完成（UI/流程 Draft），尚未串接即時生產資料
zh.region: 泰國廠區（Hon Chuan FD Packaging）
zh.problem_background: 工廠目前缺乏一套完整的 MES 系統，各機台的排程、標準工時、實際工時、在製品狀態、品質缺陷、稼動與停機資訊，多依賴人工填報或事後整理 Excel，資料即時性不足，跨部門（印刷、組裝、檢驗等）也缺乏統一的資訊平台，難以支撐即時決策與長期產能規劃。
zh.core_problem: 如何在不一次投入大型系統開發的前提下，先完成完整系統的架構與介面規劃，確立各模組（排程、佇列、現場操作、品質、監控、報表）的資料需求與呈現方式，再分階段實作與串接真實資料。
zh.solution: 先以完整系統範疇規劃 MES 草案，涵蓋 11 大模組：Brief & Answers（需求訪談）、Dashboard×3（三種看板呈現方式）、Login、MPS（主生產排程）、Planning、Machine Queue（機台佇列）、Job Detail & Route（工單與路徑）、Operator Run（現場操作）、Quality & Defects（品質與缺陷）、Monitor & Downtime（稼動與停機）、Reports（報表）；其中「生產總覽」模組已完成三種看板框架（Station board／Machine wall／Bottleneck first），並以草稿資料呈現 Plan/Actual/Waste/OEE 等關鍵指標與依站別（Print/Slice/Glue/Inspect/Perf/Slitting）的在製品（WIP）看板，做為後續與真實生產資料串接的介面基礎。
process: 進行需求訪談與問題釐清（Brief & Answers）
規劃系統整體架構與模組範疇（MPS、Planning、Machine Queue、Job Detail & Route、Operator Run、Quality & Defects、Monitor & Downtime、Reports）
設計「生產總覽」看板的三種呈現框架（Station board／Machine wall／Bottleneck first）
以草稿資料驗證看板呈現邏輯（Plan/Actual/Waste/OEE、站別 WIP 看板）
（後續）依模組優先順序分階段串接真實生產資料與機台連網

協助設計生產總覽看板的多種呈現框架，並以草稿資料驗證呈現邏輯

建立後續分階段實作與資料串接的參考藍圖

en.title: Manufacturing Execution System Master Plan Draft (HCFD MES — Full System Draft)
en.summary: A full-scope Manufacturing Execution System (MES) draft planned for the Shrink Sleeve/Label/Convert production lines, covering the complete set of modules from data entry, production scheduling, machine queueing, job routing, floor operations, and quality/defects through to uptime/downtime monitoring and reporting. The interface draft has been completed, and the "Production Overview" module already shows a real-time Plan/Actual/Waste/OEE dashboard and a station-level work-in-progress (WIP) board.
en.author: Pongwish Kampetch
en.status: System draft design completed (UI/process draft); not yet connected to live production data
en.problem_background: The plant currently lacks a complete MES system. Scheduling, standard and actual working hours, WIP status, quality defects, and uptime/downtime information for each machine mostly rely on manual reporting or after-the-fact Excel compilation, leaving data far from real-time. There is also no unified information platform across departments (printing, assembly, inspection, etc.), making it hard to support real-time decisions and long-term capacity planning.
en.core_problem: How to first complete the architecture and interface plan for a full system — establishing the data requirements and presentation approach for each module (scheduling, queueing, floor operations, quality, monitoring, reporting) — without committing to a large system build all at once, then implement and connect real data in stages.
en.solution: Planned a full-scope MES draft first, covering 11 major modules: Brief & Answers (requirements interview), Dashboard×3 (three dashboard presentation styles), Login, MPS (Master Production Schedule), Planning, Machine Queue, Job Detail & Route, Operator Run, Quality & Defects, Monitor & Downtime, and Reports. The "Production Overview" module has completed three dashboard frameworks (Station board / Machine wall / Bottleneck first) and uses draft data to present key metrics such as Plan/Actual/Waste/OEE and a station-level (Print/Slice/Glue/Inspect/Perf/Slitting) WIP board, serving as the interface foundation for connecting real production data later.
process: Conducted requirements interviews and problem clarification (Brief & Answers).
Planned the overall system architecture and module scope (MPS, Planning, Machine Queue, Job Detail & Route, Operator Run, Quality & Defects, Monitor & Downtime, Reports).
Designed three presentation frameworks for the "Production Overview" dashboard (Station board / Machine wall / Bottleneck first).
Verified the dashboard presentation logic with draft data (Plan/Actual/Waste/OEE, station-level WIP board).
(Next) Connect real production data and network the machines in stages, by module priority.

features.name: Production Overview dashboard
features.desc: Shows key metrics in real time: Plan·Shift, Actual, Waste % (with target comparison), OEE (broken down into A/P/Q), and the number of running machines.

features.name: Three dashboard frameworks
features.desc: Station board (WIP by station), Machine wall (by machine), and Bottleneck first — switchable based on the on-site use case.

features.name: Station-level WIP board
features.desc: Lists jobs, machines, progress, and exception status (e.g. waiting on material, downtime, web break) by station — Print/Slice/Glue/Inspect/Perf/Slitting.

features.name: Full module planning
features.desc: Covers the entire system scope: scheduling (MPS/Planning), machine queueing, job routing, floor operations, quality defects, uptime/downtime, and reporting.

ai_usage: Helped conduct the system requirements interviews and problem clarification, organizing them into a structured module plan.
Helped design the system's interface draft and information architecture (IA), covering all 11 modules.
Helped design multiple presentation frameworks for the Production Overview dashboard and verified the presentation logic with draft data.

tools.name: Claude (Anthropic AI assistant)
tools.desc: System architecture planning, interface draft design, and dashboard logic design.

results: Completed the module plan and interface draft for the full MES system scope (11 major modules).
Completed three framework designs for the "Production Overview" dashboard and verified feasibility with draft data.
Established a reference blueprint for staged implementation and data integration going forward.

value.name: For the business unit
value.desc: Clarifies the full system scope and each module's requirements up front, avoiding repeated direction changes during later development.

value.name: For customers
value.desc: Helps improve capacity transparency, quality traceability, and delivery accuracy over the long term.

value.name: For the company
value.desc: Validates the system design with a low-cost interface draft first, reducing the risk of formal MES development and rollout.

extensions: The three Production Overview dashboard frameworks can serve as a reference template for MES dashboards at other plants or lines.
Each module (machine queue, job routing, quality defects, etc.) can be developed independently in stages and gradually connected into a full system.
Could be integrated in the future with existing OEE, production monitoring, quality/waste, and bottleneck-analysis dashboards as data sources feeding a single MES platform.
limitations: Currently only an interface draft with sample data; not yet connected to real production data.
Machine networking (e.g. Samkoon HMI via MQTT) and each module's database still need to be built in stages.
Some machines use non-Samkoon HMIs (such as PanelMaster) and will need additional compatibility planning.
en.success_key: Planning the interface draft against the full system scope first and validating the dashboard presentation logic, giving later staged development a clear blueprint to follow and avoiding rework and scope creep from building and redesigning at the same time.

zh.title: 生產計畫團隊任務管理系統（Planning Team Task Management）
zh.summary: 為生產計畫團隊建立的 Kanban 任務管理系統，讓團隊成員能共同管理專案與任務進度（Idea／Planning／In Progress／Review），加快跨人員協作速度、提升時間與成本效率，並將內部工作分配透明化。
zh.author: Pongwish Kampetch
zh.status: 已完成，團隊日常使用中
zh.region: 泰國廠區（Hon Chuan FD Packaging）
zh.problem_background: 生產計畫團隊同時推動多項專案（如 MES、標籤機台升級、產線佈局優化等），過去缺乏統一的任務管理工具，工作分配與進度多靠口頭溝通或個別記錄，容易造成資訊落差、進度不透明，也難以快速掌握團隊整體工作量與優先順序。
zh.core_problem: 如何讓多位團隊成員共同追蹤專案與任務進度，同時兼顧不熟悉系統工具人員的易用性，並清楚呈現優先順序（Urgent/High/Medium/Low）與負責人。
zh.solution: 建立 Kanban 式任務管理系統（Planning_Team_Tasks.html），以看板欄位（Idea／Planning／In Progress／Review 等）呈現各專案與任務進度，支援指派負責人（Assignee）與備援人員（Backup）、優先順序標籤與截止日期；並針對非技術背景人員簡化操作介面，搭配泰文使用手冊，方便團隊快速上手。

團隊成員依看板欄位（Idea → Planning → In Progress → Review）拖曳更新進度
管理層可一目了然掌握團隊整體工作量與各專案完成度

en.title: Planning Team Task Management System
en.summary: A Kanban-style task management system built for the production planning team, letting team members jointly track project and task progress (Idea / Planning / In Progress / Review). It speeds up cross-team collaboration, improves time and cost efficiency, and makes internal work allocation transparent.
en.author: Pongwish Kampetch
en.status: Completed, in daily use by the team
en.problem_background: The production planning team runs multiple projects at once (such as MES, label machine upgrades, line layout optimization, etc.). In the past there was no unified task management tool — work assignment and progress relied mostly on verbal communication or individual notes, which easily led to information gaps, unclear progress, and made it hard to quickly grasp the team's overall workload and priorities.
en.core_problem: How to let multiple team members jointly track project and task progress, while keeping it easy to use for people unfamiliar with software tools, and clearly showing priority (Urgent/High/Medium/Low) and the person responsible.
en.solution: Built a Kanban-style task management system (Planning_Team_Tasks.html) that shows each project's and task's progress across board columns (Idea / Planning / In Progress / Review, etc.), supporting an assignee and a backup person, priority tags, and due dates. The interface was simplified for non-technical users and paired with a Thai-language user manual so the team could get up to speed quickly.
process: Create project cards (e.g. MES, Layout Optimization, Label Sticker Printer, etc.).
Break tasks down and assign an owner, backup, priority, and due date.
Team members drag cards across the board columns (Idea → Planning → In Progress → Review) to update progress.
Management can see the team's overall workload and each project's completion at a glance.

features.name: Kanban board
features.desc: Shows project and task progress across columns such as Idea/Planning/In Progress/Review.

features.name: Task assignment
features.desc: Lets users set an assignee and a backup owner.

features.name: Priority tags
features.desc: Urgent/High/Medium/Low color coding for quickly spotting key tasks.

features.name: Project completion display
features.desc: Each project card shows the task completion ratio (e.g. 1/3 tasks · 33%).

features.name: Simplified interface and Thai manual
features.desc: Lowers the learning curve for users unfamiliar with the system.

ai_usage: Helped design a simplified user interface to lower the barrier for non-technical users.
Produced the Thai-language user manual and team management instructions.
Helped plan the board columns and data structure to match the team's actual workflow.

tools.name: Claude (Anthropic AI assistant)
tools.desc: System interface design and Thai-language user manual production.

results: Made internal work allocation transparent, reducing information gaps caused by verbal communication.
Progress and completion for each project (e.g. MES, Layout Optimization, Label Sticker Printer, BL09, BK07, etc.) can be checked in real time.
Improved cross-team collaboration speed, supporting faster time- and cost-efficiency decisions.

value.name: For the business unit
value.desc: The production planning team can coordinate resources and track project priorities faster, improving overall execution efficiency.

value.name: For customers
value.desc: More efficient internal project management indirectly supports delivery and quality commitments.

value.name: For the company
value.desc: Improves transparency of internal work allocation and time/cost efficiency, strengthening the team's competitiveness on time and cost.

extensions: The same Kanban structure can be replicated for project management needs in other departments.
Could be further connected with other dashboards (such as MES or OEE) to form an integrated view of projects and production data.
limitations: Currently an internal team tool; board status still needs to be maintained manually as data updates.
Not yet automatically linked to production system data; priority and progress still need to be judged and updated manually.
en.success_key: Designing a simplified interface around the team's real collaboration pain points and pairing it with a Thai manual to lower the barrier to use, so even members unfamiliar with software tools could get up to speed quickly and the tool truly became part of daily work.

zh.title: 無菌飲料一廠(PET1線) 生產排程編輯器
zh.summary: 一套線上生產排程編輯工具，可新增/修改批次與充填時段，於明細中選取棧板紙料號並鍵入需求箱數，並以甘特圖呈現整體排程，完成後可一鍵產出 PDF，方便現場與相關單位查閱、留存排程結果。
zh.author: 陳聖如
zh.status: 開發完成，供現場排程調整與查閱使用
zh.region: 台灣
zh.problem_background: PET1 線的月排程過去多以 Excel 或紙本方式製作與調整，遇到批次異動時，產量（噸）、箱數、板面數等數據需要人工重新試算，過程繁瑣且容易出錯，相關單位也不易即時查看最新排程結果。
zh.core_problem: 如何讓排程調整更直覺、資料自動運算，並方便將排程結果輸出留存與分享給相關單位查閱。
zh.solution: 以網頁形式打造可視化的生產排程編輯器，透過甘特圖呈現批次與充填時段，並自動依輸入的箱數換算產量（噸）、板面數等數據，讓排程調整與查閱更即時、直覺。
process: 盤點原有 7 月排程資料與排程邏輯（批次、產品、充填時段、棧板紙料號等欄位）
使用 Claude Code 協助開發網頁應用，建立排程資料結構與甘特圖介面
實作批次新增/編輯、產量與板面數自動計算、PDF 匯出等功能

en.title: Aseptic Beverage Plant 1 (PET1 Line) Production Schedule Editor
en.summary: An online production schedule editor for adding and editing batches and filling time slots, selecting the correct pallet paper spec and entering required case counts in the detail view, and visualizing the whole schedule as a Gantt chart. The finished schedule can be exported to PDF with one click for the plant floor and related teams to review and keep on record.
en.author: Chen Sheng-Ju
en.status: Development complete, in use on the floor for schedule adjustment and lookup
en.problem_background: The monthly schedule for the PET1 line was previously built and adjusted mostly in Excel or on paper. Whenever a batch changed, figures such as output (tons), case counts, and pallet-face counts had to be recalculated by hand — a tedious, error-prone process — and related teams could not easily see the latest schedule.
en.core_problem: How to make schedule adjustments more intuitive, have the numbers recalculate automatically, and make it easy to export and share the resulting schedule with related teams.
en.solution: Built a web-based, visual production schedule editor that displays batches and filling time slots as a Gantt chart, and automatically derives output (tons), pallet-face counts, and other figures from the entered case counts — making schedule adjustments and lookups more immediate and intuitive.
process: Reviewed the existing July schedule data and scheduling logic (batch, product, filling time slot, pallet paper spec, and other fields).
Used Claude Code to help build the web app, establishing the schedule data structure and the Gantt chart interface.
Implemented batch creation/editing, automatic output and pallet-face calculation, and PDF export.
Deployed to Netlify for internal use and testing.

features.name: Schedule Gantt chart
features.desc: Shows each batch's filling start/end time on a timeline, with expand-all/collapse-all views.

features.name: Batch creation and editing
features.desc: Add batches, edit filling time slots, and in the detail view select the pallet paper spec and enter the required case count.

features.name: Automatic statistics
features.desc: Instantly calculates total batch count, total output (cases/tons), and number of product SKUs.

features.name: Reset to original schedule
features.desc: One click restores the original July schedule, making it easy to compare before/after adjustments.

features.name: PDF export
features.desc: Exports the current schedule as a PDF document.

ai_usage: Used Claude Code to help plan the web app architecture and write the scheduling logic and Gantt chart front-end code.
AI helped turn the scheduling rules (output, case count, and pallet-face conversions) into automatically calculated web app functionality.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.desc: Helped design and build the entire schedule editor web app.

tools.name: Netlify
tools.desc: Website deployment and hosting.

results: When the schedule changes, the Gantt chart and statistics update in sync instantly, removing the need to manually recalculate output, case counts, and pallet-face counts.
The schedule can be exported to PDF with one click, making it easy for the floor and related teams to keep records, review, and communicate.

value.name: For the business unit
value.desc: Schedulers can adjust batches and filling time slots faster, with total output and pallet-face statistics available at a glance.

value.name: For the company
value.desc: Reduces manual recalculation work and the risk of errors, improving the transparency and flow of production schedule information.

extensions: The same schedule editor architecture can be extended to production schedule management for other lines or plants.
Could later be connected to the actual production database, replacing the current manual data entry.
limitations: Data is currently auto-saved only in the local browser; clearing the browser cache or switching devices may lose the schedule data, so exporting PDFs periodically is recommended.
Not yet connected to a formal production or ERP system — schedule data still needs to be entered and maintained manually.
en.success_key: Built on the actual July schedule data used on the floor, with the Gantt chart and automatic calculations mirroring schedulers' existing workflow, which lowered the adoption barrier.

zh.title: 跨國員工績效自評與多階主管評核 Web App
zh.summary: 運用 Google Sheets、Google Apps Script 與網頁前端技術，建立一套適用於東南亞多國據點的員工績效考核系統。系統支援員工個人化 KPI、自評、Leadership／Individual 差異化評分、多階 Reviewer 依序評核、主管平均給分及多語言介面；員工不需具備公司 Google 帳號，即可透過工號與 PIN 登入完成考核。
zh.unit_request: 東南亞總部人力資源單位
zh.unit_owner: 東南亞總部人力資源單位
zh.author: 禤珮宜
zh.status: 已完成可操作測試版本，持續進行多語言配對、權限規則與正式上線驗證
zh.region: 東南亞六國據點：柬埔寨、緬甸、越南、泰國、印尼、馬來西亞，以及總部管理端
zh.problem_background: 公司各國廠區人數差異大，單一據點約 13 至 400 人，且並非所有員工都有公司 Google 帳號。考核 KPI 採逐人設定，每位員工的 KPI 項目、權重與 Reviewer 路徑皆可能不同；Reviewer 1 至 Reviewer 3 必須依序評核，且 Reviewer 與 Reviewee 不一定隸屬相同廠區。原先以 Google Form 規劃時，難以同時處理個人化 KPI、自動帶入員工資料、差異化評分、多階簽核及跨國語言需求，而付費 AppSheet 亦不符合專案的成本條件。
zh.core_problem: 如何在不增加軟體授權成本、員工沒有公司 Google 帳號的條件下，建立一套能支援個人化 KPI、跨廠區多階主管依序評核、不同職務定位評分公式、多語言操作、資料追蹤及重複送出控管的績效考核工具。
zh.solution: 以 Google Sheets 作為資料庫，搭配 Google Apps Script Web App 建立員工自評與 Reviewer 評核兩套網頁介面。資料結構拆分為員工主檔、KPI 指派、登入權限、自評主檔、自評明細、Reviewer 主檔、評核指派、主管評核主檔及 KPI 評核明細等工作表；員工與 Reviewer 以 ID、PIN 及啟用狀態登入。系統依 Employee Type 自動套用評分架構，並以 Submission ID、Reviewer Level、狀態欄位與伺服器端驗證維持流程順序和資料完整性。
process: 釐清制度規則：確認 KPI 採逐人設定、評分範圍為 0 至 100 的整數，以及 Leadership／Individual 的評分組成。
建立 Google Sheets 資料架構：完成 01_Employee_Master 至 09_KPI_Review_Response 等主檔、指派表與結果表。
建立員工登入與自評頁面：透過 Emp ID 與 Access PIN 登入，自動顯示基本資料與個人 KPI。
建立兩頁式自評流程：第一頁填寫 KPI，第二頁填寫 Teamwork 及依 Employee Type 決定是否顯示 Leadership。
建立送出前檢核：驗證必填欄位、整數分數、KPI 權重及加權後的自評總分。
建立 Reviewer 管理與評核流程：設定 Reviewer 1 至 3，依序開放待評案件，並顯示員工自評與前階 Reviewer 紀錄。
建立最終評分邏輯：各階 Reviewer 獨立留存分數與評語，完成後以所有 Reviewer 分數平均作為主管評核平均給分。
建立多語言介面：支援 English、Thai、Vietnamese、Malay、Nepali、Indonesian、Burmese、Khmer，並依各國需求搭配中文或英文。
進行錯誤排除與測試：處理 Spreadsheet ID、欄位名稱、百分比格式、送出按鈕、重複送出、員工類型及工作表同步等問題。
建立手動同步功能：由 01_Employee_Master 將新增的 Active 員工安全地補入 03_Access_Control 與 07_Review_Assignment，不重排或覆蓋既有資料。
儲存程式、執行 testConfiguration、更新 Web App deployment，並以不同員工類型與 Reviewer 層級進行端到端測試。

en.title: Cross-Border Employee Performance Self-Evaluation & Multi-Level Manager Review Web App
en.summary: Built with Google Sheets, Google Apps Script, and web front-end technology, this is an employee performance evaluation system for multiple sites across Southeast Asia. It supports per-employee personalized KPIs, self-evaluation, differentiated scoring for Leadership vs. Individual roles, sequential multi-level reviewer evaluation, averaged manager scoring, and a multi-language interface. Employees can complete the evaluation by logging in with their employee ID and PIN, without needing a company Google account.
en.author: Xuan Pei-Yi
en.status: Working test version complete; ongoing work on multi-language pairing, permission rules, and go-live validation
en.region: Six Southeast Asia sites (Cambodia, Myanmar, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia) plus HQ administration
en.problem_background: Plant headcount varies widely across countries, from about 13 to 400 people per site, and not every employee has a company Google account. KPIs are configured per individual employee, so each employee's KPI items, weights, and reviewer path can differ; Reviewer 1 through Reviewer 3 must evaluate in sequence, and a reviewer and reviewee are not necessarily at the same plant. A Google Forms-based design struggled to handle personalized KPIs, auto-populated employee data, differentiated scoring, multi-level sign-off, and cross-border language needs at the same time, while paid AppSheet did not fit the project's cost constraints.
en.core_problem: How to build a performance evaluation tool that supports personalized KPIs, sequential multi-level manager review across plants, different scoring formulas by employee type, multi-language operation, data tracking, and duplicate-submission control — without adding software licensing cost and without employees having a company Google account.
en.solution: Google Sheets serves as the database, paired with a Google Apps Script Web App that provides two web interfaces: employee self-evaluation and reviewer evaluation. The data model is split across sheets including the employee master, KPI assignment, login access control, self-evaluation master and detail, reviewer master, review assignment, manager review master, and KPI review detail; employees and reviewers log in with an ID, PIN, and active status. The system automatically applies the right scoring structure based on Employee Type, and uses a Submission ID, Reviewer Level, and status fields together with server-side validation to keep the workflow order and data integrity intact.
process: Clarified the policy rules: confirmed KPIs are set per employee, scores are whole numbers from 0 to 100, and defined the Leadership vs. Individual scoring composition.
Built the Google Sheets data architecture: completed master sheets, assignment sheets, and result sheets from 01_Employee_Master through 09_KPI_Review_Response.
Built the employee login and self-evaluation page: employees log in with Emp ID and Access PIN, which auto-displays their basic info and personal KPIs.
Built a two-page self-evaluation flow: page one for KPIs, page two for Teamwork and, depending on Employee Type, Leadership.
Built pre-submission checks: validation of required fields, whole-number scores, KPI weights, and the weighted self-evaluation total score.
Built reviewer management and review flow: configured Reviewer 1 through 3, opened pending cases in sequence, and displayed the employee's self-evaluation plus prior reviewers' records.
Built the final scoring logic: each reviewer level keeps its own score and comments independently, and once all reviewers are done, their scores are averaged into the manager review score.
Built the multi-language interface: supports English, Thai, Vietnamese, Malay, Nepali, Indonesian, Burmese, and Khmer, paired with Chinese or English depending on the country's needs.
Debugged and tested: resolved issues with Spreadsheet ID, field names, percentage formatting, submit button behavior, duplicate submissions, employee type handling, and sheet synchronization.
Built a manual sync function: safely adds newly Active employees from 01_Employee_Master into 03_Access_Control and 07_Review_Assignment without reordering or overwriting existing data.
Saved the code, ran testConfiguration, updated the Web App deployment, and ran end-to-end tests across different employee types and reviewer levels.

value.desc: Centralizes previously scattered employee, KPI, reviewer, and review-result data, reducing the manual effort of compiling, tracking, and consolidating spreadsheets.

value.name: For employees
value.desc: No company Google account needed to use the system, and personal data, KPIs, component scores, and the total score can all be clearly confirmed before submission.

value.name: For managers
value.desc: Provides a clear to-do list, visibility into prior review stages, and a consistent scoring interface that supports sequential review across plants.

value.name: For the company
value.desc: Establishes a low-cost, traceable, replicable, cross-border performance evaluation process that improves policy consistency and data transparency.

extensions: Duplicating the whole Google Sheet along with its bound Apps Script creates an independent version for the next half-year review cycle.
Employee Master, KPI Assignment, and Review Assignment can be adjusted to quickly apply the system to different countries, plants, or headcounts.
Can be extended with a formal return-for-revision flow, HR reopening, email notifications, overdue reminders, and a progress dashboard.
Can add attendance, core competencies, values, talent review, or calibration-meeting dimensions to the evaluation.
The same ID/PIN login, personalized questions, and multi-level review architecture can extend to training needs surveys, probation reviews, promotion evaluations, and internal application processes.
The multi-language dictionary can be maintained independently, and other country languages or a different secondary display language can be added later.
limitations: Google Apps Script is still subject to daily quotas, per-execution time limits, and high concurrent access; scenario testing at peak headcount should be done before go-live.
PIN is a lightweight login mechanism, not enterprise-grade SSO; access to the Google Sheet, Apps Script, and deployment must be restricted to necessary administrators.
Emp ID, Reviewer ID, field names, and sheet names must stay unique and consistent, or login, assignment, or data-write errors can occur.
Each employee's Active KPI weights must total 100%, and the Weight cell format must be consistent to avoid double-converting values like 35 and 35%.
Adding new employees currently requires manually running syncEmployeeRecords rather than an automatic trigger; HR still needs to set PIN, active status, and reviewers afterward.

If a submitted evaluation needs changes, simply resetting the status to Not Submitted is not enough — it can create a new Submission ID and duplicate detail rows; a formal Reopen flow should be built instead.
After editing Code.gs, Index.html, Reviewer.html, or Translations.html, a New version must be created and redeployed, or the live URL won't load the new version.
Multi-language text should be reviewed by HR or native speakers in each country to ensure the policy terminology and local meaning are correct.
After duplicating the Google Sheet, still check the Spreadsheet ID, deployment, authorization, URL, and data-clearing scope to avoid carrying over sensitive data from the previous cycle.
en.success_key: Define the performance policy rules, employee positioning, scoring formulas, reviewer order, and data ownership clearly before starting development; keep sheet fields standardized, enforce key validation on the server side, and run full end-to-end tests across different countries, employee types, and reviewer levels. HR needs to retain governance responsibility for the master data, access control, reviewer assignment, and version deployment for this low-cost tool to keep running reliably over the long term.

zh.title: 清新廠倉儲部出勤自動統計範本
zh.summary: 將清新廠倉儲部叉車組原本逐人、逐日人工判讀的出勤整理工作，製作成可每月重複使用的 Excel 公式範本。使用者設定月份並貼入系統匯出資料後，即可依已提供的每日紀錄彙總出勤天數、無出勤天數與日期備註，並另外查看缺卡提醒及需人工確認的例外。已交付含資料的測試版本、空白範本與操作說明。
zh.author: 徐喬奎
zh.problem_background: 倉儲部取得出勤系統匯出的 Excel 檔後，原本需要人工逐日查看每位員工的打卡時間與請假註記，再整理成工號、姓名、出勤天數、無出勤天數及日期備註的月度表格。來源資料除了早班、常日班，也包含夜班、跨日打卡及多次打卡紀錄，無法單靠是否有兩筆打卡判斷全日出勤。
zh.core_problem: 同樣有上下班打卡，仍可能因請假而只計半天出勤；只有一筆打卡，也不能直接認定為未出勤。新進人員可能只有部分月份的紀錄，未提供資料的日期不應自動補算為無出勤。每月更新資料時，還需要避免舊資料、人工調整或重複紀錄影響結果，並讓彙總數字能回查到每日原始紀錄。
zh.solution: 建立不使用 VBA 的 .xlsx 公式範本，分為「月度彙總」與「出勤明細」兩張工作表。明細保留系統匯出的 A～S 欄，在右側計算每日出勤、無出勤、日期備註及異常提示，並提供獨立的人工調整欄與調整原因。月度彙總依工號加總當月已提供的紀錄，將缺卡提醒與無出勤分開呈現。另提供已清除人員資料、統計月份與人工調整的空白範本，讓使用者可直接貼入新的月份資料。
process: 讀取系統匯出的 .xls 檔，確認工作表、19 個來源欄位、日期範圍及每人每日紀錄的結構。
與需求方確認統計規則，包括單筆打卡且無請假計出勤 1 天，缺卡提醒另外保留。
依請假時數、打卡資料與班別建立每日判斷公式，將資料矛盾或無法辨識的情況列為需人工確認。
建立「出勤明細」與「月度彙總」，以八月人工提供的統計結果逐人核對天數與日期備註。
使用七月資料測試新進人員情境，將原本要求完整月份紀錄的檢查，改為只加總已提供紀錄，不補算未提供日期。
測試人工調整、零值調整、缺少調整原因、重複紀錄、部分月份與未知請假情況，並以 LibreOffice 重算核對輸出。
交付空白範本與操作說明，驗證貼入資料後可重新計算，並確認空白檔未殘留員工資料。

features.name: 月度自動彙總
features.desc: 依工號整理姓名、出勤天數、無出勤天數、日期備註及核對狀態。

features.name: 半天出勤判斷
features.desc: 依 4 小時請假紀錄配合打卡計算 0.5 天出勤，並在支援的日班情境辨識上午或下午請假。

features.name: 缺卡提醒
features.desc: 檢查第一卡至第四卡及來源異常註記；單筆打卡且無請假仍計出勤 1 天，提醒另外保留。

features.name: 部分月份統計
features.desc: 新進人員只計算實際提供的紀錄，不將沒有資料的日期補算為無出勤。

features.name: 人工調整留痕
features.desc: 提供人工出勤、人工時段與調整原因欄位，保留原始資料及自動判斷結果。

features.name: 匯入與例外檢查
features.desc: 檢查重複工號日期、缺少工號、無效日期、其他月份資料與殘留人工調整。

features.name: 空白範本重複使用
features.desc: 預設支援 1,000 筆每日紀錄與 40 位員工，保留公式、下拉選單、格式及操作說明。

ai_usage: 使用 Codex 讀取來源表格，辨識欄位結構與打卡、請假及跨日紀錄的差異。
將需求方確認的判斷方式轉換成 Excel 公式與人工確認流程。
協助產生試算表、核對人工參考結果，並測試公式在不同輸入條件下的反應。
指出來源資料與人工預期不一致的案例，保留待確認事項，避免為符合總數而推定未提供的請假日期或規則。
AI 用於範本設計與驗證；日常統計由 Excel 公式執行，不需要每月將資料重新交由 AI 判讀。

tools.name: Codex
tools.desc: 需求釐清、來源資料檢查、公式設計、程式產製與測試協作。

tools.name: Microsoft Excel
tools.desc: 作為使用者設定月份、貼入資料、查看彙總及填寫人工調整的操作介面。

tools.name: @oai/artifact-tool
tools.desc: 產生 .xlsx 檔案、設定公式與格式，並渲染工作表供畫面檢查。

tools.name: Python
tools.desc: 讀取舊版 .xls 來源、核對原始資料、檢查輸出檔與資料保留情況。

tools.name: LibreOffice
tools.desc: 對輸出的 .xlsx 進行獨立重算與結果核對。

results: 已交付含資料的出勤統計測試版本、依已提供紀錄計算的修正版，以及可直接貼入資料的空白範本。
八月來源包含 10 位員工、310 筆紀錄；出勤、無出勤天數及日期備註與需求方提供的八月參考表一致。
七月來源包含 10 位員工、282 筆紀錄；新進人員的 3 筆紀錄可正常彙總為出勤 3 天、無出勤 0 天。
修改部分月份計算方式後，八月回歸核對結果維持一致；未提供日期不再阻擋彙總或自動補算無出勤。
已測試空白範本的月份提示、貼入資料後計算及清除後回復空白狀態，並檢查輸出檔沒有殘留員工資料。
已完成公式與 LibreOffice 重算核對；七月仍有兩筆與人工預期不同的結果，已列出差異及所需確認資訊。

value.name: 對需求單位
value.desc: 可將逐人、逐日的重複計算改為貼入資料後核對彙總，集中處理例外與需人工確認的紀錄。

value.name: 對負責單位
value.desc: 將出勤判斷方式落實為可查看的公式與操作說明，方便後續維護及討論規則調整。

value.name: 對公司
value.desc: 保留來源、判斷與人工調整原因，讓統計結果可追溯，並提供其他相同格式作業可參考的範本。

extensions: 相同匯出欄位與統計規則的其他月份，可直接使用空白範本更新資料。
其他班組若採用相同來源格式，可先確認班別與出勤規則，再套用此整理方式。
後續可依需求擴充支援筆數、人數及班別判斷，但須同步調整公式範圍並重新驗證。
若希望減少複製貼上的操作，可再評估 Power Query 或選檔匯入功能；目前交付版本仍採手動貼入資料。
limitations: 首次使用先在「月度彙總」B4 輸入當月日期，再將來源 Table1 的 A～S 欄資料，不含標題，以「只貼值」貼至「出勤明細」A10。
重複使用已填資料的檔案時，先清除篩選，再清除 A10:S1009 與 V10:X1009 的內容；不要刪除整列、整欄或使用全部清除，也不要覆蓋公式欄。
統計僅反映當月已提供紀錄；沒有某日紀錄不代表該日無出勤，也不代表來源一定完整。
單筆打卡且無請假計出勤 1 天，是本次需求已確認的規則；若涉及前一日夜班下班卡重複帶入隔日，仍須另行確認。
4 小時假配合打卡計 0.5 天，8 小時假且無打卡計 0 天；其他時數或互相矛盾的紀錄需人工確認。
半天時段自動判斷目前限支援的早班與常日班情境；夜班、跨日或無法辨識的情況，須補上人工時段與原因。
七月仍有兩筆差異待需求方確認：一筆額外半天無出勤的日期與依據，以及一筆隔日單卡是否僅為前一日夜班下班卡。這兩項尚未納入新的自動扣減規則。
範本支援 1,000 筆紀錄、40 位員工；超出範圍前應先擴充，並保留系統原始日期順序。
目前未建立自動匯入、VBA 按鈕或線上服務；也尚未量測實際節省工時，或完成需求單位使用環境的正式驗收。
zh.success_key: 先以實際匯出資料與需求方提供的參考結果確認規則，再將每日判斷、月度加總與人工例外處理分開。特別區分「有紀錄但無打卡」與「沒有提供紀錄」，以及「缺卡提醒」與「無出勤」，讓新進人員及不完整打卡不會被同一套簡化判斷誤算。對尚未確認的差異保留原因與追查方向，不用推測補足結果。

en.title: Automated Attendance Statistics Template for Qingxin Plant Warehouse
en.summary: Turned the Qingxin Plant warehouse forklift team's manual, person-by-person and day-by-day attendance review into a reusable monthly Excel formula template. After setting the month and pasting in the system export, users get attendance days, non-attendance days, and date notes summarized from the daily records provided, with missing-punch reminders and exceptions needing manual review shown separately. A test version with data, a blank template, and operating instructions have been delivered.
en.author: Hsu Chiao-Kuei
en.problem_background: After receiving the Excel file exported from the attendance system, the warehouse department had to manually review each employee's punch times and leave notes day by day, then compile a monthly table of employee ID, name, attendance days, non-attendance days, and date notes. Besides morning and regular day shifts, the source data also includes night shifts, cross-day punches, and multiple punches, so full-day attendance cannot be judged simply by whether there are two punches.
en.core_problem: An employee with both clock-in and clock-out may still count as only half a day due to leave; a single punch cannot be treated as absence. New hires may have records for only part of the month, and dates with no records should not be counted as non-attendance automatically. Each monthly update also needs to prevent old data, manual adjustments, or duplicate records from skewing results, while keeping every summary figure traceable to the original daily records.
en.solution: Built a VBA-free .xlsx formula template with two sheets: Monthly Summary and Attendance Detail. The detail sheet keeps the system export's columns A–S and calculates daily attendance, non-attendance, date notes, and anomaly hints to the right, with separate manual-adjustment and reason columns. The monthly summary totals the month's provided records by employee ID and shows missing-punch reminders separately from non-attendance. A blank template with personnel data, statistics month, and manual adjustments cleared is also provided so users can paste in a new month's data directly.
process: Read the system-exported .xls file and confirmed the worksheet, 19 source columns, date range, and per-person daily record structure.
Confirmed statistics rules with the requesting unit, including that a single punch with no leave counts as 1 attendance day, with a missing-punch reminder kept separately.
Built daily judgment formulas based on leave hours, punch data, and shift, flagging contradictory or unrecognizable cases for manual review.
Built the Attendance Detail and Monthly Summary sheets and verified days and date notes person by person against the manually prepared August results.
Tested the new-hire scenario with July data, changing the check that required full-month records to one that only totals provided records without filling in missing dates.
Tested manual adjustments, zero-value adjustments, missing adjustment reasons, duplicate records, partial months, and unknown leave cases, and cross-checked output by recalculating in LibreOffice.
Delivered the blank template and instructions, verified recalculation after pasting data, and confirmed no employee data remained in the blank file.

features.name: Automatic monthly summary
features.desc: Compiles name, attendance days, non-attendance days, date notes, and check status by employee ID.

features.name: Half-day attendance
features.desc: Counts 0.5 day when a 4-hour leave record coincides with punches, and identifies morning or afternoon leave for supported day shifts.

features.name: Missing-punch reminders
features.desc: Checks punches 1–4 and source anomaly flags; a single punch with no leave still counts as 1 day, with the reminder kept separately.

features.name: Partial-month statistics
features.desc: New hires are counted only on records actually provided; dates without data are not counted as non-attendance.

features.name: Audit trail for manual adjustments
features.desc: Provides manual attendance, manual time-slot, and reason columns while preserving the original data and automatic results.

features.name: Import and exception checks
features.desc: Detects duplicate ID-date pairs, missing IDs, invalid dates, other-month data, and leftover manual adjustments.

features.name: Reusable blank template
features.desc: Supports 1,000 daily records and 40 employees by default, keeping formulas, dropdowns, formatting, and instructions.

ai_usage: Used Codex to read the source table and identify the column structure and differences between punch, leave, and cross-day records.
Converted the judgment rules confirmed by the requesting unit into Excel formulas and a manual review process.
Helped generate the spreadsheet, check against manual reference results, and test formula behavior under different inputs.
Pointed out cases where source data and manual expectations disagreed, keeping open questions instead of inferring unprovided leave dates or rules just to match totals.
AI was used for template design and validation; routine statistics run on Excel formulas, with no need to send data to AI each month.

tools.name: Codex
tools.desc: Requirements clarification, source data inspection, formula design, file generation, and test collaboration.

tools.name: Microsoft Excel
tools.desc: Interface for setting the month, pasting data, viewing summaries, and entering manual adjustments.

tools.name: @oai/artifact-tool
tools.desc: Generates the .xlsx file, sets formulas and formatting, and renders sheets for visual checks.

tools.name: Python
tools.desc: Reads legacy .xls sources, checks raw data, and inspects output files and data retention.

tools.name: LibreOffice
tools.desc: Independently recalculates the output .xlsx to cross-check results.

results: Delivered a test version with data, a revised version that calculates only on provided records, and a blank template ready for pasting data.
The August source covers 10 employees and 310 records; attendance days, non-attendance days, and date notes match the August reference table provided by the requesting unit.
The July source covers 10 employees and 282 records; a new hire's 3 records correctly summarize to 3 attendance days and 0 non-attendance days.
After changing the partial-month logic, August regression results remained consistent; missing dates no longer block the summary or get counted as non-attendance.
Tested the blank template's month prompt, calculation after pasting data, and return to a blank state after clearing, and confirmed no employee data remained in the output file.
Completed formula and LibreOffice recalculation checks; two July results still differ from manual expectations, with the differences and needed information listed.

value.name: For the requesting unit
value.desc: Replaces repetitive per-person, per-day counting with pasting data and reviewing the summary, focusing effort on exceptions and records needing manual confirmation.

value.name: For the owning unit
value.desc: Captures the attendance rules as viewable formulas and instructions, making later maintenance and rule discussions easier.

value.name: For the company
value.desc: Keeps sources, judgments, and manual adjustment reasons so results are traceable, and offers a reference template for other tasks using the same format.

extensions: Other months with the same export columns and rules can be updated directly with the blank template.
Other teams using the same source format can apply this approach after confirming their shift and attendance rules.
Record counts, headcount, and shift logic can be expanded as needed, but formula ranges must be adjusted and re-verified.
To reduce copy-and-paste, Power Query or file-picker import could be evaluated later; the delivered version still uses manual pasting.
limitations: On first use, enter the month's date in Monthly Summary B4, then paste columns A–S of source Table1 (without headers) as values only into Attendance Detail A10.
When reusing a filled file, clear filters first, then clear the contents of A10:S1009 and V10:X1009; do not delete whole rows or columns, use Clear All, or overwrite formula columns.
Statistics reflect only the records provided for the month; a missing record for a date does not mean absence, nor that the source is complete.
Counting a single punch with no leave as 1 day is a rule confirmed for this request; cases where a previous night shift's clock-out carries into the next day still need separate confirmation.
A 4-hour leave with punches counts as 0.5 day, and an 8-hour leave with no punches counts as 0 days; other hours or contradictory records require manual review.
Automatic half-day time-slot detection currently supports only morning and regular day shifts; night shifts, cross-day, or unrecognizable cases need a manual time slot and reason.

Two July differences await confirmation from the requesting unit: the date and basis of one extra half-day of non-attendance, and whether one next-day single punch is only the previous night shift's clock-out. Neither has been added as a new automatic deduction rule.
The template supports 1,000 records and 40 employees; expand it before exceeding these limits, and keep the system's original date order.
No automatic import, VBA button, or online service has been built; actual time savings have not been measured, and formal acceptance in the requesting unit's environment is not yet complete.
en.success_key: Rules were first confirmed against actual export data and the reference results provided by the requesting unit, then daily judgment, monthly totals, and manual exception handling were kept separate. The template explicitly distinguishes "a record with no punch" from "no record provided," and "missing-punch reminder" from "non-attendance," so new hires and incomplete punches are not miscounted by one oversimplified rule. Unconfirmed differences are kept with their reasons and follow-up direction rather than filled in by guesswork.

zh.title: 東南亞 SO/DN/WO 營運資料分析平台（SEA SODNWO）
zh.summary: 把東南亞各子公司從 ERP 匯出的 SO（銷售訂單）、DN（送貨單）、WO（工單報工）Excel 報表，集中上傳到同一個網站平台，經過驗證後自動彙整成接單、出貨、生產的分析儀表板，讓東南亞總部與管理層可依國家、公司、據點逐層查看營運狀況；平台上每一個數字都能追溯回原始 Excel 的那一列，不使用任何假資料或估計值。
zh.author: 徐喬奎
zh.region: 東南亞（泰國、越南、馬來西亞、印尼、緬甸、柬埔寨，共 35 個據點）
zh.problem_background: 東南亞各國子公司的接單、出貨與生產報工資料都存在 ERP 中，要看整體營運狀況時，只能由各單位各自匯出 Excel，再人工彙整成報表。各國幣別不同（THB、VND、MYR、IDR、MMK、USD），同一張單重新匯出後也容易重複計算，管理層很難即時、一致地掌握全區、各國、各公司、各據點的接單金額、出貨進度與生產良率，更難回頭查證某個數字是從哪一份檔案、哪一列來的。
zh.core_problem: 如何把分散在各國、格式一致但分次匯出的 SO/DN/WO Excel 報表，安全地匯入同一個平台，自動去重、換算幣別，並依使用者權限提供從集團到單一據點的營運分析，同時確保每個數字都真實、可追溯。
zh.solution:
以 React Router（SSR）+ Cloudflare Workers + D1 + R2 建立一個網站平台：
- 管理者上傳 SO/DN/WO Excel 後，系統先「預覽驗證」（必填欄位、Loc ID 是否已登記、是否重複檔案、新增/修訂/未變更筆數），完全不寫入資料；全部通過後才「確認匯入」，任何一份檔案有問題整批都不寫入。

en.title: SEA SO/DN/WO Operations Data Analytics Platform (SEA SODNWO)
en.summary: Sales order (SO), delivery note (DN) and work order production report (WO) Excel exports from the ERP of each Southeast Asia subsidiary are uploaded to a single web platform, validated, and automatically consolidated into order, shipment and production dashboards. Southeast Asia Headquarters and management can drill down by country, company and site, and every number on the platform can be traced back to the exact row of the original Excel file — no mock data or estimates are ever used.
en.author: Mark Hsu
en.region: Southeast Asia (Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Myanmar, Cambodia — 35 sites in total)
en.problem_background: Order, shipment and production report data for each Southeast Asia subsidiary lives in the ERP. To see overall operations, each unit had to export Excel files and consolidate them into reports by hand. Currencies differ by country (THB, VND, MYR, IDR, MMK, USD), and re-exporting the same document easily led to double counting. Management found it hard to get a timely, consistent view of order amounts, shipment progress and production yield across the region, each country, company and site — and even harder to verify which file and which row a given number came from.
en.core_problem: How to safely import SO/DN/WO Excel reports — same format but exported separately by each country — into one platform, automatically de-duplicate and convert currencies, and provide operations analysis from group level down to a single site according to user permissions, while making sure every number is real and traceable.
en.solution:
A web platform built with React Router (SSR) + Cloudflare Workers + D1 + R2:
- After an administrator uploads SO/DN/WO Excel files, the system first runs a preview validation (required columns, whether each Loc ID is registered, duplicate-file detection, counts of new / revised / unchanged rows) without writing any data. Only when everything passes can the batch be confirmed; if any file has a problem, nothing in the batch is written.
- The ERP's Line Rec Key is the unique identity of every line, so re-exporting a document only creates a new revision instead of double counting. Original Excel files are stored permanently in R2, and every line can be traced back to its source file, worksheet and row number.
- SO amounts use each country's home currency and are converted to the reporting currency with site-wide shared exchange rates; when a rate is missing, the amount is clearly marked as "not included" rather than filled with 0.
- Dashboards switch across four scope levels — Group → Country → Company → Site — and visible data is filtered by the countries, companies and sites each user is authorized for.
process: Confirmed the SO/DN/WO source Excel formats and analysis needs with Southeast Asia Headquarters, and built a Loc ID registry of 35 sites with their country and company assignments
Designed the data model: import batches, raw-row snapshots, line identities and revisions, shared exchange rates, accounts and three-level permissions
Developed Excel parsing and a two-step import flow (upload & preview → confirm import), with a real progress bar and whole-batch voiding
Built the Overview, Orders & Shipments, Production, Period Comparison, Region / Company / Site analysis and Document Detail pages
Deployed to Cloudflare Workers, with a daily automatic database backup via GitHub Actions
Continuously refined charts, currency conversion and company structure based on feedback from Southeast Asia Headquarters

extensions: The same "two-step import + Line Rec Key revisioning + raw-row traceability" architecture can be reused for ERP report analysis in Taiwan, China and other regions
Can be extended to more ERP report types (e.g. inventory, purchasing, accounts receivable) to become a regional operations overview
AI-generated analysis summaries or anomaly detection could be added on top of the real data in the future, while keeping every number traceable
limitations: Data depends on units regularly exporting and uploading Excel files from the ERP; there is no direct ERP integration yet, so freshness depends on upload frequency
Every Loc ID in an uploaded file must already be registered in the site table, otherwise the whole batch is blocked; new sites must be registered by an administrator first
SO exports have no currency column, so amount conversion relies on each country's home-currency setting and the shared exchange rates, which users must maintain
Data upload and batch voiding are administrator-only; accounts with only company / site permissions (no country-level grant) cannot see region-wide totals
en.success_key: A strict rule that "every number on screen comes from real, imported data": Line Rec Key identity prevents double counting, batches are written only when all validation passes, original Excel files are kept permanently and traceable row by row, and missing data is shown honestly rather than filled in — so management can make decisions with confidence in the platform's numbers.

zh.title: THC LINE Insight：LINE 群組訊息 AI 分析平台
zh.summary: 廠內與業務單位每天在 LINE 群組回報設備異常、生產批次、品管檢查、開機率、客戶專案進度等資訊，但這些訊息散落在聊天紀錄中，事後很難查找、統計與追蹤。LINE Insight 讓官方帳號加入既有的 LINE 群組，自動收下每一則訊息，由 AI 依群組類型萃取成結構化資料（異常事件、生產批次、專案進度、待辦議題等），再以 Dashboard 呈現 KPI、趨勢、排行與時間軸。現場人員不用改變任何回報習慣，管理者就能從「翻聊天紀錄」變成「看儀表板」。
zh.author: 徐喬奎
zh.region: 集團各廠區與業務單位（含台灣及海外據點，支援中文、泰文、英文等多語訊息）
zh.problem_background: LINE 群組是廠內與業務單位最習慣、最即時的溝通工具：設備異常、產線生產狀況、品管檢查結果、各廠開機率、客戶專案進度，大多直接在群組裡回報。但聊天紀錄是流水帳，訊息一多就被洗掉；想知道「這台設備這個月壞了幾次」「哪些專案卡住需要主管決策」「哪個單位今天還沒回報」，都只能靠人工往回翻、再整理成 Excel。海外據點的群組還會混雜泰文、英文，閱讀門檻更高。
zh.core_problem: 如何在不改變現場人員既有 LINE 回報習慣、不要求大家另外填表的前提下，把群組裡的非結構化對話自動轉成可查詢、可統計、可追蹤的管理資訊？
zh.solution:
建立 LINE 官方帳號並加入各單位既有的 LINE 群組，透過 Webhook 即時接收訊息（文字、圖片），由 AI 依照群組套用的「分析模板」萃取成結構化資料，存進資料庫後以 Dashboard 呈現。目前提供 7 種分析模板，新群組只要選擇合適的模板即可使用，不需另外開發：
- 一般（設備異常分析）：萃取異常事件，統計設備異常排行、故障 Pareto 與機台狀態
- 日報（客戶專案進度）：追蹤客戶專案狀態、AI 標記風險與待主管決策事項、主管指示與重要日期
- 生產回報（多單位開機率彙整）：彙整各廠開機率、回報完成率、設備與品質異常
- 產線 Mini-MES：還原產線生產批次、CIP/SIP 製程與異常事件的時間軸
- 異常事件分析：把同一設備的多則處理進度訊息合併成一個事件追蹤到結案
- 產線 Mini-MES 2.0：解析格式化的生產批次回報、品管檢查與機台班報
- 群組工作總覽：追蹤綜合型群組中的各項議題、待確認事項與排程公告

群組依類別（廠區／部門）分組，使用者依權限只能看到自己被授權的類別。

AI 信心度不足的判斷進入人工審核佇列，由管理者確認或修正
使用者登入 Dashboard 依期間、類別篩選，查看 KPI、趨勢圖、排行與時間軸，並可一鍵回溯原始對話
