en.title: Physiological Evaluation for the Respiratory Protection Program
en.summary: AI helped review the respiratory protection program and turn the decision on whether to refer someone to a physician into three steps. The physiological evaluation results for 28 respirator wearers were compiled into one table, with a separate case-by-case explanation of each decision, serving as the nurse's record and the basis for discussions with safety staff and the on-site physician.
en.author: 陳佳勳
en.problem_background: Under the respiratory protection program, people who need to wear respirators must have a physiological evaluation before use to confirm they are fit to wear one, with referral to a physician when needed. Deciding whether to refer requires looking at questionnaire answers, personal medical history, and the load imposed by the task and respirator together.
en.core_problem: Referral criteria are scattered across regulatory appendices, the technical manual and company procedures, and it isn't easy to tell which are legally mandatory and which are company discretion. Checking each person's evaluation form one by one takes time and makes it hard to apply the same standard to everyone; once done, there was no at-a-glance summary table, and the reasons behind each decision weren't recorded.
en.solution: AI reviewed the respiratory protection program and organized the referral decision into three sequential steps, marking whether each step is legally mandatory or company discretion. The 28 wearers' evaluation results were then organized by these steps into one table, with the reason for each decision written down, and used after the nurse confirmed them.
process: The nurse provides the respiratory protection program and wearers' physiological evaluation data
AI reviews the program, extracts the referral criteria and separates legal requirements from company discretion
Simplify the criteria into three steps, confirmed by the nurse
Organize the 28 wearers' results by the three steps into one summary table
Write a case-by-case explanation of each decision, marking the nurse's extended judgments
The nurse reviews before use, and uses it for discussions with safety staff and the on-site physician

features.name: Step 1 (legal requirement)
features.desc: If the questionnaire ticks any ※-marked item in Appendix 3 (e.g. epilepsy, heart disease history, stroke, angina, heart failure) → refer directly, no discretion

features.name: Step 2 (technical guideline, company discretion)
features.desc: No history in the five major categories—cardiovascular, respiratory, neurological, musculoskeletal, psychiatric → no referral, no need to check task load

features.name: Step 3 (company discretion)
features.desc: For those with Step 2 history, check whether the task and respirator are high-load (e.g. SCBA, heat level 3 or above, emergency response to strongly corrosive chemicals, moderate-to-heavy work) → not high-load: no referral; high-load: referral recommended

features.name: Evaluation summary table
features.desc: Respirator type, workload, decision and reason for all 28 wearers in one table, color-coded by decision, with physician evaluation results recorded

features.name: Case-by-case decision explanation
features.desc: Records the reason for each case, and separately marks the nurse's extended judgments based on risk reasonableness that aren't explicitly covered by the manual or company procedure

ai_usage: Reading the respiratory protection program to find conditions relevant to referral
Separating legally mandatory conditions from company discretion
Organizing scattered conditions into sequential steps
Organizing each person's results by the steps and compiling them into a table
Writing the case-by-case decision explanations

en.success_key: First organize the decision criteria clearly—separating legal requirements from company discretion—and have the nurse confirm them, then apply them to each person and record the reason for every case. AI does the organizing; fitness decisions stay with professionals.

zh.title: 肌肉骨骼症狀調查分析
zh.summary: 以 AI 分析四廠 561 份肌肉骨骼症狀調查問卷，依官方指引自動判定疑似有危害的人員並統計人數，產出健康管理名單。每廠分析時間由 2 天縮短為 1 小時內。

zh.region: 台灣（四廠：無菌一廠、無菌二廠、無菌三廠、自貿廠）
zh.problem_background: 依職業安全衛生法規，公司需推動人因性危害預防計畫，其中一步是請員工填寫肌肉骨骼症狀調查表，針對頸、肩、手、背、膝、腳等 15 個身體部位的不適程度評分，再依官方指引找出疑似有危害的人員做進一步評估。問卷結果匯出為 Excel 後，需要逐筆檢視每個人 15 個部位的分數。
zh.core_problem: 過去由職護以 Excel 人工逐筆檢視、判定並統計，每廠需要約 2 天。問卷匯出的資料格式不乾淨（例如分數是文字格式無法直接計算），各廠欄位也略有不同，人工處理費時又容易漏看。
zh.solution: 由職護提供問卷匯出檔與官方指引，請 AI 先讀指引原文確認判定標準，再清理資料、逐筆判定每位員工的危害等級，產出包含疑似有危害名單、全體分析與統計摘要的健康管理名單。完成後由 AI 以獨立計算逐筆複核，第一廠確認後其餘各廠沿用同一版型。

en.title: Musculoskeletal Symptom Survey Analysis
en.summary: AI analyzed 561 musculoskeletal symptom questionnaires from four plants, automatically identifying people with suspected hazards according to official guidelines, counting them and producing health management lists. Analysis time per plant dropped from 2 days to under 1 hour.
en.author: 陳佳勳
en.status: Completed (Aug–Sep 2026; lists delivered for all four plants)
en.region: Taiwan (four plants: Aseptic Plants 1, 2 and 3, and the Free Trade Zone Plant)
en.problem_background: Under occupational safety and health regulations, the company must run an ergonomic hazard prevention program. One step is asking employees to fill in a musculoskeletal symptom survey, rating discomfort in 15 body areas such as the neck, shoulders, hands, back, knees and feet, then using official guidelines to identify people with suspected hazards for further evaluation. After the survey is exported to Excel, each person's 15 scores have to be reviewed one by one.
en.core_problem: Nurses previously reviewed, judged and counted each record manually in Excel, taking about 2 days per plant. The exported data was messy (e.g. scores stored as text that couldn't be calculated), and columns differed slightly between plants, so manual work was slow and error-prone.
en.solution: The nurse provided the survey exports and official guidelines. AI first read the original guideline text to confirm the criteria, then cleaned the data, judged each employee's hazard level, and produced health management lists including a suspected-hazard list, full analysis and statistical summary. AI then re-checked every record with an independent calculation; once the first plant was confirmed, the other plants used the same template.
process: The nurse prepares each plant's survey export and the Ergonomic Hazard Prevention Program Guidelines
AI reads the original guideline text to confirm the criteria, confirmed by the nurse
AI checks and cleans data formats (text-formatted scores, extra characters in headers, etc.) without ever modifying the original files
AI judges each record's hazard level and counts people by body area and department
AI produces the health management list in Excel and re-checks every record with an independent calculation
The nurse confirms the scope (e.g. whether to include staff from other plants) and the results as the basis for follow-up evaluation

zh.title: 風險地圖熱力圖分析
zh.summary: 將稽核缺失的資料以熱力圖呈現在廠區的風險地圖上，讓主管一眼就能看出廠區中缺失集中的區域，作為安排重點管理與改善的依據。
zh.author: 謝欣錫
zh.region: 宏全一廠、宏全二廠
zh.problem_background: 過去主管只能逐筆查看稽核紀錄，再自行推測缺失集中在廠區的哪些區域。紀錄以文字或表格呈現，無法一眼看出缺失的分布與熱點，難以判斷應優先加強管理的區域。
zh.core_problem: 稽核缺失缺乏空間化的呈現方式，主管無法直觀掌握缺失熱點，難以重點呈現需要管理區域。
zh.solution: 使用 Claude 協助開發「異常位置熱力圖累積工具」，以單一 HTML 檔製作，開啟就能使用。將 IRP 稽核資料匯出的 Excel 載入工具後，系統會依缺失的位置標示在廠區圖上，並把一段期間（例如一個月）的缺失累積疊加，次數越多顏色越深，讓主管一眼就能看出缺失熱點。

主管檢視熱力圖，找出缺失集中區域並安排重點管理

en.title: Risk Map Heatmap Analysis
en.summary: Audit findings are displayed as a heatmap on the plant's risk map, so managers can see at a glance which areas have concentrated findings and use this to plan focused management and improvements.
en.author: 謝欣錫
en.region: Hon Chuan Plant 1, Hon Chuan Plant 2
en.problem_background: Managers previously had to review audit records one by one and guess which plant areas had concentrated findings. Records were presented as text or tables, making it impossible to see the distribution and hotspots of findings at a glance, or to decide which areas needed stronger management first.
en.core_problem: Audit findings lacked a spatial presentation, so managers could not intuitively grasp hotspots or highlight the areas that needed management.
en.solution: Claude helped develop the "Abnormal Location Heatmap Accumulation Tool" as a single HTML file that works as soon as it is opened. After loading the Excel exported from the IRP audit system, the tool marks each finding's location on the plant map and accumulates findings over a period (e.g. one month). The more findings, the darker the color, so managers can spot hotspots at a glance.
process: Export audit findings for the chosen period from the IRP system (Excel)
Open the Abnormal Location Heatmap Accumulation Tool (HTML file)
Load the Excel data; the tool maps each finding's location onto the plant map
The tool accumulates findings from the same period to generate a heatmap
Managers review the heatmap, identify areas with concentrated findings and arrange focused management

zh.title: 東南亞六國多語言績效考核系統
zh.summary: 以 Google Sheets 作為資料後台、Google Apps Script Web App 作為員工與主管的操作介面，取代原本「Excel 訂 KPI → Google Form 自評 → HR 人工整理 → 主管 Excel 評核」的流程。沒有公司信箱的員工也能用工號與 PIN 自行登入自評，主管依序評核，並支援雙語介面、評語翻譯、進度通知與各廠成績同步。
zh.author: 禤珮宜
zh.status: 已完成可操作版本，持續試填與修正中
zh.region: 柬埔寨、緬甸、越南、泰國、印尼、馬來西亞（共 10 個廠區）
zh.problem_background: 原本的考核分散在 Excel、Google Form 與 HR 人工整理之間，KPI 設定、自評、主管評分到最終結果沒有串成完整的資料鏈。HR 需要反覆複製、轉貼與追蹤，主管要在不同表單間作業，員工也不容易確認自己適用的項目與完成狀態。六國語言不同、管理層級不同，部分現場員工也沒有公司信箱；加上需付費的 AppSheet 無法採用，因此改以既有的 Google 工具自行建置。
zh.core_problem: 考核資料靠人工在多個表單間銜接，容易遺漏與版本不一致；沒有公司信箱的員工無法自行填寫，主管評核也無法控制先後順序，跨國語言差異更增加了操作難度。
zh.solution: 採用「中央資料後台＋員工自評入口＋主管評核入口＋各廠成績輸出」的架構。Google Sheets 儲存員工主檔、KPI 指派、自評、主管評核、草稿、翻譯快取與寄信紀錄；Apps Script 依登入身分與員工類型提供個人化的 KPI 與表單，並控制送出與流轉。員工完成自評後，案件依序交給第一、二、三階主管獨立評分，最後以實際完成主管的加權總分平均產生最終分數，再由中央系統單向同步到各廠成績活頁簿。過程中以 AI 協助產出與修正程式、翻譯資源、測試與操作指南。

員工填寫個人 KPI、Teamwork 與 Leadership（適用者）自評，可暫存草稿，檢查後送出
主管以主管編號＋PIN 登入，查看待評核清單、員工自評與前階紀錄，必要時翻譯評語
第一、二、三階主管依序獨立評分並送出，系統自動流轉並計算最終平均分數
HR 透過各廠追蹤活頁簿掌握進度，成績由中央系統同步到各廠 Final sheet

limitations: 六國正式上線、全部廠區同步驗收與整體結案尚未完成確認
尚未量化節省的工時、錯誤率降低或使用滿意度
後台欄位名稱不可任意更改，否則程式會找不到表單或欄位
員工主檔、員工類型、KPI 權重與主管對應須由 HR 確保正確
程式修改後須重新部署新版本，正式網址才會套用
評語機器翻譯涉及評核判斷時，主管仍應核對原文語意
各廠檔案需分別設定權限，IMPORTRANGE 與共用資料夾本身不提供完整資料隔離
目前未做正式負載測試，大量同時使用需依 Apps Script 配額另行驗證
zh.success_key: 由 HR 持續主導制度與操作規則，先解決員工本人填寫、無信箱登入、個人 KPI、主管依序評核與計分等核心需求，再依試填結果逐步加入草稿、資料更正、翻譯與進度追蹤。以使用者提供的真實畫面與錯誤反覆驗證，介面調整先模擬再實作；並將歷史設計、已交付程式與未驗收項目分開管理，讓單一測試版能複製為六國可持續使用的流程。

en.title: Multilingual Performance Appraisal System for Six Southeast Asian Countries
en.summary: Using Google Sheets as the data backend and a Google Apps Script Web App as the interface for employees and managers, this system replaces the old flow of "KPIs set in Excel → self-evaluation via Google Form → manual HR processing → manager review in Excel". Employees without a company email can log in with their employee ID and PIN to complete self-evaluations, managers review in sequence, and the system supports bilingual interfaces, comment translation, progress notifications and score syncing to each plant.
en.author: 禤珮宜
en.status: Working version completed; trial use and refinement ongoing
en.region: Cambodia, Myanmar, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia (10 plants in total)
en.problem_background: Appraisals were previously split across Excel, Google Forms and manual HR processing, so KPI setting, self-evaluation, manager scoring and final results never formed a complete data chain. HR had to copy, paste and chase repeatedly, managers worked across different forms, and employees struggled to confirm which items applied to them and whether they were done. The six countries differ in language and management levels, and some frontline employees have no company email. With paid AppSheet not an option, the system was built with existing Google tools.
en.core_problem: Appraisal data was manually passed between multiple forms, leading to omissions and version inconsistencies; employees without company email could not fill in forms themselves, the order of manager reviews could not be controlled, and language differences across countries made operation even harder.
en.solution: The system uses a "central data backend + employee self-evaluation portal + manager review portal + per-plant score output" architecture. Google Sheets stores the employee master, KPI assignments, self-evaluations, manager reviews, drafts, translation cache and email logs; Apps Script serves personalized KPIs and forms based on the logged-in identity and employee type, and controls submission and routing. After an employee submits, the case passes in order to Reviewer 1, 2 and 3 for independent scoring; the final score is the average of the weighted totals from the reviewers who completed it, and the central system then syncs scores one-way to each plant's score workbook. AI helped produce and fix code, translation resources, tests and user guides throughout.
process: HR prepares this period's employee master, employee types, KPIs and weights, reviewer assignments and login PINs
Employees choose a language, log in with employee ID + PIN and confirm their basic data first (if wrong, they submit a correction request and pause)
Employees complete self-evaluations of personal KPIs, Teamwork and Leadership (where applicable), can save drafts, then check and submit
Reviewers log in with reviewer ID + PIN, view their pending list, the employee's self-evaluation and earlier reviews, and translate comments when needed
Reviewers 1, 2 and 3 score independently in sequence; the system routes cases automatically and calculates the final average score
HR tracks progress through per-plant tracking workbooks, and scores are synced from the central system to each plant's Final sheet

features.name: Employee ID + PIN login
features.desc: No company email needed; employees log in and self-evaluate themselves

features.name: Personalized KPIs
features.desc: Shows each employee's applicable KPI items and weights from backend assignments

features.name: Sequential manager review
features.desc: Reviewer 1 → 2 → 3 score independently in order; later reviewers can see earlier records

features.name: Role-based scoring
features.desc: Individual: KPI 80% + Teamwork 20%; Leadership: KPI 60% + Teamwork 20% + Leadership 20%

features.name: Drafts and data correction
features.desc: Manual and automatic saving to resume later; employees with wrong basic data submit a correction request for HR

features.name: Lock after submission
features.desc: Prevents duplicate self-evaluations and edits after submission; Reviewer 1 must confirm the performance interview is done

features.name: Eight bilingual interfaces
features.desc: English, Thai, Vietnamese, Malay, Nepali, Indonesian, Burmese and Khmer, each paired with Chinese or English

features.name: Comment translation
features.desc: Reviewers can translate employee comments into Traditional Chinese or English on demand, keeping the original and caching results

features.name: Batch notifications and HR summary
features.desc: Combines emails to reviewers and HR by time slot, logging send status to prevent duplicates

features.name: Plant tracking and score sync
features.desc: Plant HR sees its own progress and incomplete items; scores sync one-way from the center to 10 plant workbooks

ai_usage: Broke down HR's cross-country appraisal process into system specs for login, self-evaluation, routing, review, notification and sync
Helped compare Google Forms, AppSheet and Apps Script to choose a feasible approach
Produced Apps Script, HTML/CSS/JavaScript and plant sync code step by step based on rules confirmed by the user
Located issues from screenshots and error messages provided by the user, repeatedly fixing field names, statuses, translations and email links
Generated eight bilingual interfaces and notification text, and mocked up UI changes for confirmation before changing the live version
Prepared employee and reviewer user guides (Word) and a training deck (PPT)

tools.desc: Central data backend storing the master data, appraisal results, drafts and email logs

tools.name: Google Apps Script
tools.desc: Login verification, routing, scoring, syncing and scheduling

tools.name: Apps Script Web App
tools.desc: Browser portals for employee self-evaluation and manager review

tools.name: LanguageApp
tools.desc: Machine translation of comments on the reviewer side

tools.name: MailApp
tools.desc: Batch notification emails to reviewers and HR

tools.name: IMPORTRANGE
tools.desc: Lets plant tracking workbooks read headquarters data

tools.name: ChatGPT / Codex
tools.desc: Requirements, code collaboration, debugging, translation resources and user guides

tools.name: Word / PowerPoint
tools.desc: Employee and reviewer user guides and training deck

results: Working version of employee self-evaluation and manager review completed, covering login, personal KPIs, sequential review, role weights and final average
Added drafts, data correction, lock after submission, interview confirmation, pending-list refresh and completed overview
Set up progress tracking and separate score workbooks for 10 plants, and delivered the one-way sync program
Provided batch emails, HR completion summaries and email logs (scheduled emails are currently paused; manual sending is kept)
Produced bilingual Chinese/English user guides for employees and reviewers, plus a combined training deck

value.name: For employees
value.desc: Can self-evaluate without a company email, see personal KPIs in a familiar language and finish in several sittings

value.name: For managers
value.desc: See self-evaluations and earlier reviews in one place, score independently at each level and translate comments instantly

value.name: For plant HR
value.desc: Get their plant's progress and scores directly, reducing manual linking and follow-up

value.name: For headquarters HR
value.desc: Govern appraisals across six countries with consistent fields, scoring and flow, reducing the risk of mixed versions

value.name: For the company
value.desc: A half-yearly appraisal process built on existing Google tools that can be reused, with the full review history preserved

extensions: Copy a new appraisal file each half year and update the master data, KPIs and reviewers to reuse it
New plants can be added by reusing the plant routing and permission logic
Designs such as ID + PIN login, drafts, correction requests, sequential approval and email logs can serve as a reference for other internal approval flows
The employee and reviewer guides can be updated with languages and real screenshots and reused for training
limitations: Official go-live in all six countries, sync acceptance for all plants and overall closure have not yet been confirmed
Time saved, error reduction and user satisfaction have not yet been quantified
Backend field names must not be changed freely, or the program will not find sheets or fields
HR must keep the employee master, employee types, KPI weights and reviewer assignments correct
After code changes, a new version must be deployed for the live URL to apply them
When machine-translated comments affect review judgments, reviewers should still check the original meaning
Each plant's files need their own permissions; IMPORTRANGE and shared folders do not provide full data isolation
No formal load test has been done; heavy concurrent use must be verified against Apps Script quotas
en.success_key: HR continuously led the rules and procedures, first solving the core needs—employees filling in their own forms, login without email, personal KPIs, sequential manager review and scoring—then gradually adding drafts, data correction, translation and progress tracking based on trial results. Real screenshots and errors from the user were used for repeated verification, UI changes were mocked up before implementation, and historical designs, delivered code and unaccepted items were managed separately, turning a single test version into a process all six countries can keep using.
